criteria.text: test_body_limit_rejects_oversized_streaming_body_without_content_length: a body without Content-Length that exceeds max_body_size gets a plain-text 413 'Content Too Large'; multipart uploads are counted by raw bytes including encoding overhead.

test_body_limit_content_length_failfast, test_body_limit_understated_content_length, test_body_limit_exactly_at_limit_allowed: declared oversized length is rejected before the app reads the body; an understated header does not bypass the limit; a body of exactly max_body_size passes.

test_body_limit_no_double_response: when the limit is crossed after the response has started, no second http.response.start is sent and receive raises HTTPException(413); inside Starlette the standard handler yields 413 when the response has not started.
test_body_limit_scope_key: MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY == 'starlette.max_body_size', holds the effective limit while the app runs, and the previous value or its absence is restored afterwards.
test_max_body_size_param_on_starlette_router_mount_route: each of the four accepts max_body_size and enforces it; the default None leaves requests unlimited.

test_app_level_limit_applies_to_middleware_reading_body: Starlette(max_body_size=N) with a user middleware reading the body gets 413 above N; Content-Length fail-fast applies even when the endpoint never reads the body.

test_inner_limit_raises_outer and test_inner_limit_lowers_outer: Route, Mount or Router limits override the app limit in both directions, including a declared Content-Length above the outer limit but within the inner one.
test_multipart_closes_temp_files_on_any_interruption: when the stream raises (for example HTTPException or a generic exception) mid-multipart, all SpooledTemporaryFiles created are closed.
Middleware is pure ASGI (no BaseHTTPMiddleware); nothing new is exported from starlette/__init__.py. 413 text is the literal 'Content Too Large'.

intents.rationale: Content-Length fail-fast plus byte counting in the middleware.
Track response-started state by wrapping send; raise HTTPException(413) from receive.
Constant and scope set/restore in the middleware.
Keyword missing on all four classes.
Starlette.build_middleware_stack must insert the limit middleware before user middleware.
Route/Mount/Router wrap their app with the middleware, which rebases on the original receive.
Cleanup only catches MultiPartException and OSError today.

summary: Add a pure-ASGI body-limit middleware first, then make multipart temp-file cleanup robust (independent), then wire max_body_size into Starlette/Router/Mount/Route. Inner limits override outer ones by re-wrapping the original receive. The app-level Content-Length fail-fast has to be deferred until routing, so that an inner route can raise the limit. Without deferral, the outer check would reject the request first.

tasks.summary: Create starlette/middleware/body_limit.py: MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY and RequestBodyLimitMiddleware(app, max_body_size). It wraps receive with a counting wrapper that remembers the original receive and the count so far, so a nested instance can rebase on the original receive with its own limit. It fail-fasts on Content-Length with PlainTextResponse('Content Too Large', 413). It tracks response-started by wrapping send. It raises HTTPException(413) from receive on overflow, and sends the 413 itself only if the response has not started. It sets and restores the scope key (try/finally; absent key is deleted). It also needs an internal option to defer the Content-Length fail-fast (used by the Starlette app-level instance in T3).
In MultiPartParser.parse, close all files in _files_to_close_on_error on any BaseException (not just MultiPartException/OSError) and re-raise; add a test using a stream that raises mid-upload.

Add the max_body_size keyword to Starlette, Router, Mount and Route. Starlette inserts the middleware (deferred fail-fast) just after ServerErrorMiddleware and before user middleware. Router, Mount and Route wrap their app with RequestBodyLimitMiddleware when set, so the inner limit rebases the receive and overrides the outer one. When no inner limit exists, the effective scope-key limit's Content-Length fail-fast is still applied at route entry, so endpoints that never read the body are rejected. Add tests for all four classes, including raising and lowering the limit.
